notes.title: Rise of the Village Hero 1.0 – Now Complete + New Videos!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Thank you so much to everyone who has purchased my game in the last couple of days. Your support means a lot to me.

As I mentioned in my earlier update, my game is now fully complete. I'll be keeping the feedback form in the game so you can report any bugs or share your thoughts. I've tested the game extensively, so it should hopefully be as bug-free as possible.

The demo will also remain available for the foreseeable future, featuring the first level and a few smaller areas. I want you to be completely satisfied with your purchase, so I encourage you to try the demo first—it will give you a good idea of what the game has to offer.

To submit feedback on my game, you have a couple of options:


 Press F12 inside the game's demo or the full release to access the feedback form. You can then enter your feedback subject and details in the provided fields.
 Join my Discord and head over to the 'Feedback Ideas Suggestions' channel. Drop your suggestions or feedback there, and I'll do my best to respond promptly.


How I may address/ respond to your feedback: 


 I may send you an email if you've provided one in the feedback form (though it's not required).
 I’ll also respond to any questions in my Discord as soon as possible.
 Additionally, I've created a YouTube playlist where I'll address suggestions and feedback, as well as share tutorials and tips on how to survive in Rise of the Village Hero. Link below.



Here's the latest feedback video:
[previewyoutube=5i90EZqtcS8;full][/previewyoutube]

Thank you once more for your support—I hope you have a great time with version 1.0!

Silviu

notes.title: Mid March update
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Quick mid-month update. I’ve managed to upload Chapter 4, which is now quite close to the final version of the game. I’m so excited to see it all coming together! Here’s what’s been added:


 Completed all levels for Chapter 4 (I’ll double-check things, and more polish may be added).
 Added all quests and dialogues for Chapter 4.
 Linked NPCs in Chapter 4 with previously completed quests.
 Introduced new weapons for enemies in chapter 3 and chapter 4. New enemies for chapter 4.
 Expanded armour and weapon selection with more shields and axes.
 Enhanced the polish of Desma City’s poor and rich quarters.
 Added or corrected descriptions for swords and made numerous other improvements.


For the rest of the month, here’s my plan:

 Testing the Steam build to evaluate quest and level completion, checking weapons, descriptions, quests—basically everything.
 Uploading any patches to address issues as I discover them.


Please provide feedback if you encounter any bugs or have suggestions.
I’m getting close to version 1.0, and I honestly can’t wait for you all to experience the finished game. I’ll continue testing and work on balancing enemies, player levels, equipment availability, stores, gold—basically everything.

Thank you so much for your support.

— Silviu

notes.title: Februrary Update Patch
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Just a quick update: I've noticed that shops were buying items nearly at full price, so I've adjusted the purchase prices. Players will now receive only 50% or sometimes 30% depending on the location. Of course, you can use your charisma points to improve these rates.

I plan to do more testing to ensure this balances well with item prices and the overall gameplay experience. I want players to enjoy visiting new shop locations without feeling that items have no value because they can buy everything. It'll take some tweaking, and I'll continue testing it.

I've also added Chapter 4, Desma City, which is the second level of Chapter 4 (with Dema Outskirts being the first). I'll be working on the other levels and adding them throughout the month.

I'll be adding enemies and NPCs to Desma City, but if you've reached Chapter 4 and have suggestions for NPCs—perhaps people Guy has met in the past—or ideas for quests and enemies, simply press F12 at that location to provide your suggestions.

Chapter 4 will be the final chapter. For new players, the game offers 12-14 hours of gameplay. If you take your time exploring, visiting shops, and selling items, completing all quests. Chapter 4 will extend the experience to 16-20 hours, as originally planned for early access.

Thank you all so much for your support. This month, I'll be focusing solely on Rise of the Village Hero, ensuring the game gets as close to 1.0 as possible.

See you at the next update!

Silviu

notes.title: February Month End Update - New areas, weapons and much more!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Welcome to the end of Feb update for Rise of the Village Hero! I’m thrilled to share everything I’ve been working on this month, and there’s quite a lot to cover. Let’s dive in a lot to break down.

New Bows Added: I’ve introduced a whole arsenal of new bows, each with their own model:
•	Silver Bows: Huntress, Death’s Sigh
•	Green Bows: Thunderstrike, Willow, Hatred’s Sting, Quickstrike, Barrage
•	Blue Bows: Windrunner, Death’s Kiss, Warsong
•	Light Gold Bow: Razorsong
•	Gold Bow: Devil Whisperer
•	Purple Bows: Valkyrie, Hornet’s Sting, Needle Shooter
Will need to add some proper descriptions to these.
With the addition of these bows (more to come in future updates), there are now officially two distinct playstyles in the game. You can either fight up close in true warrior fashion with a sword and shield or take down enemies from a distance with these bows. I’ve adjusted the Dexterity requirements for bows—since Guy is a hunter, it only makes sense for him to be proficient with bows and arrows, so requirements are lower for Dexterity.

On top of that, I’ve added a quiver of arrows to the player character’s back to visually reflect that he’s got arrows and ready from the very start.

New Swords Introduced: Inspired by the rich legends of Dobrogea, I’ve added several new swords to the game:
•	Sword of Eternity
•	Sword of Buceag Lake 
•	Blade of Skirtos (wielded by a famous Dacian mercenary and gladiator)
•	Blade of the White Wolf
•	Blade of the Hunter Prince 

New Armor Sets:
•	Skirtos Armor Set: Chest plate, greaves, boots, helmet, and wristbands—rewarded through different quests in Chapter 3.
•	Eternity Armor Set: The chest plate and other pieces are available in Toothless Rick’s shop at the tavern.

New Potions: I’ve expanded the potion system with medium and large versions:
•	Medium Health Potions & Large Health Potions
•	Medium Stamina Potions & Large Stamina Potions

These potions have been added to shops (mainly in Chapters 2 and 3) and as floor drops. I’ve balanced their distribution, removing some potions where I felt there were too many, but this will still require a lot of testing to get the pricing and effectiveness just right.

New Quests: Chapter 3’s Wynter Town now has a new quest from the mayor, who needs your help saving his home from an evil creature. More side quests will be added soon—there are a lot of houses players can explore, and I think a couple more adventures can fit right in.

Cinematics and Voiceovers: I’ve added new flythrough cinematics for Chapter 2 and the transition to Chapter 3 (The Long Road to Wynter). There are also new voice queues:
•	"I completed this quest" plays when a quest is finished, reminding players to check their inventory for rewards. 
•	"I got a new quest" plays when you receive a new quest, prompting you to open your quest book (press Q) and see your objectives and rewards.

These sound effects aim to improve the player experience based on your feedback. And yes—it's still my voice, since there’s no budget for a professional voice actor yet. Maybe one day!

Chapter 4: Desma – Work in Progress: : I’m excited to announce that work on Chapter 4 has officially begun! The Desma Outskirts level is already added to the build – let me know what your thoughts are - , and I’ve set up music, lighting, and visual effects. Some enemies have been placed as placeholders—though they likely won’t all be the only enemies in this area—I’ll flesh out the area with proper NPCs and dialogue soon.

What to Expect in the March Update: 
Provided testing goes well (and as any game dev knows, it usually brings up things to tweak!), here’s what I hope to focus on next:
•	Unique weapons for Chapter 3 enemies
•	Finalizing Chapter 3 with a couple more quests and more armour and item drops
•	Adding more daggers, shields, axes, maces, and possibly spears
•	Completing a majority of Chapter 4’s levels and placing temporary NPCs with some dialogue
•	Polishing existing levels to fix anything that stands out
•	Add more enticing descriptions to the new sets of armours and weapons added. 

Chapter 4 will be the final chapter I don’t think I’ll wrap everything up next month, but I’m getting close. More testing is ahead.

Thank You! 
A heartfelt thank you to everyone who purchased Rise of the Village Hero during the recent sale, and to those who’ve supported the game since its launch in January 2024. I truly appreciate every player, and I’m so grateful for the streamers—both big and small—who’ve helped spread the word about the game.
Thank you for all the feedback you’ve given me over the months. It’s helped me improve the game in so many ways. As a solo developer, your support means the world.
And if you’ve enjoyed your time with Rise of the Village Hero, please leave a review, it would help me a lot! 

See you in the next update!

Silviu

notes.title: January update - Rise of the Village Hero gets third chapter
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Thank you so much for your patience! Since returning from my holiday on January 7th, I've been hard at work on finishing Chapter 3 and getting it added to the game. I'm thrilled to announce that Chapter 3 is now officially live! Ast the game will have four chapters that is really exciting as I am getting closer to 1.0.

Here’s a breakdown of what you can expect:

New Locations:
•	Wynter Town Outside Palisade: Reintroducing Edda and her son as NPCs, and concluding the Obsidian Talons storyline, assuming you’ve allied with the Amber Blades.
•	Wynter Town Inside Palisade: Here, you can explore inside the palisade, access most of the town's houses, and venture into the Poor Quarter, where 4 houses are explorable, as well as explore the Rich Quarter where, 2 rich houses, the tavern, and the church (which is locked at the start of the chapter).
•	Wynter Town Tavern Interior: This is where many survivors have taken refuge. If you’ve helped NPCs in previous quests (like the soldier in Warlington and the farmer), you'll see them return here. They’ll share how your actions impacted their lives and how they’ve paid it forward. I’m really happy about this because it brings a sense of continuity and impact to the story, even if not all actions have major consequences. As a solo developer, I try to create as many meaningful connections as I can.
•	Wynter Town Poor Quarter: This area, once home to farmers, reflects the harsh climate of Wynter, where only root vegetables like potatoes and carrots grow. The market square brings trade from other towns.
•	Wynter Town Rich Quarter: The mayor’s house, the church, the market square, and four rich houses (two of which are explorable) are here, including the tavern.
•	Wynter Town Church: The final scene of this chapter, where defeating the evil marks the completion of Chapter 3 – Part 4 Quest. From here, you can walk through the back of the church to access Long Road to Wynter, which was previously locked. This leads to the desert and eventually to the next gate toward Chapter 4 (Desma). Since Chapter 4 isn’t finished yet, you'll get a "Thank you for playing" message at the end, but stay tuned for updates!

New Additions:
•	Enemies: A variety of new enemies have been introduced, including the Glowing Spirit Monster, Spirit Monster, Evil God (the final boss for Chapter 3), and the Red Demon (mini-boss). Red skeletons make a return as well. Glowing and Spirit Monsters are already deployed, alongside the Red Skeletons and Evil God, while I’m still working on the Red Demon mini-boss.
•	New equipment: The Skirtos Mercenary Equipment Set has been added in Chapter 3 (Part 3), and in Part 4, players can earn chest plates, greaves, and boots. The helmet and wristbands will be deployed soon.
•	More swords: A few new blades are coming soon, including the Sword of Eternity, Sword of Buceag Lake, Blade of Skirtos the Gladiator, Blade of White Wolf, and the Blade of the Hunter Prince.
I’ve tested Chapters 1-3 and everything is holding up well! Quests complete nicely, and no issues were found with the progress so far.

What to Expect in February:
•	Deploy more equipment: I’ll add more items as rewards and drops from enemies.
•	Additional Equipment: If I feel the stores are lacking, I will create and deploy new gear.
•	Testing: The first week of February will be dedicated to testing. I’ll go over the game multiple times, analyse stats like player vs. enemy balance, loot pricing, and rewards. Please don’t hesitate to press F12 to provide constructive feedback – it’s really appreciated!
•	New Potions: I’ll add Medium Stamina Potions, as well as Large Health Potions and Large Stamina Potions, both restoring double the value of the medium potions and costing double as well.
•	Additional Side Quests: Expect a few more side quests in Chapter 3.
•	Start Working on Chapter 4: I’ll begin working on the final chapter soon.
•	New Trailer Cinematic: If time allows, I’d love to create a new cinematic trailer for the game.

Thank you all so much for your incredible support throughout this journey I am one step closer now to 1.0 with chapter 3 releasing. 

Your feedback has been invaluable, and I can’t wait to keep improving the game with your help.

See you in February!

Silviu

notes.title: December Update: New abilities, armour and more!
notes.content:
Event Update: The special demo event, where players could win up to five keys, has now concluded. The demo will be reverted to its original state, containing the same scenes as before the event. Thank you to everyone who participated!

New Features and Additions:
•	Healing Chant Ability: A new ability has been introduced to reduce reliance on healing potions. Different levels of this ability are now available in all shops (up to level 8), allowing players to purchase higher levels as they progress. The Healing Chant has a cooldown period, ensuring balanced gameplay and encouraging strategic use of both the chant and potions. Consequently, healing potions will become less abundant in the world, requiring players to purchase them or manage resources wisely.

Tier 2 Armour Completion:
•	Divine Fortune Chestplate and Trousers
•	Guardian of Steel Chestplate Armour With these additions, all Tier 2 armour types are now complete. Work will now shift towards developing Tiers 3 and 4, which will be introduced in Chapters 2 and 3 and 4. This is an exciting step forward in expanding the game’s content.

New Armour Sets:
Glory of the East Set:

 	Available as rewards for Chapter 2 quests, with pieces found in Level 2 caves and Toothless Rick’s shop.
 	Toothless Rick returns in Chapter 2 as a trader.
 Wit of Heroes Set:
 	A new armour set with pieces available as drops in the Chapter 2 boss level and at Toothless Rick’s store.
 	Additional rewards can be earned from completing the “Long Road to Wynter” quest, which involves diplomatic missions with the elves.


Bug Fixes and Improvements:
•	Adjusted armour stats across various sets.
•	Corrected grammar mistakes and resolved icon duplication issues.
•	Lowered the prices of small and medium stamina and health potions to help players save money for new items in subsequent chapters.
•	Updated trader inventories to ensure they stock all new items.

Fixed minor issues, including:

 	Skeleton names for certain NPCs.
 	Grammar errors in weapon descriptions.
 	Incorrect icons (e.g., trousers showing as boots).


Chapter 2 Updates:
•	Added new story elements, including:
•	Story elements in the cave boss area and cave levels 1 and 2.
•	A new story element in the White Shallows at the Obsidian Talons camp. Which gives more hints to what the group is all about.
•	Toothless Rick has been added as a trader in Chapter 2. He is only available if you choose a non-aggressive path with the goblin conglomerate in Warlington Town.

A Heartfelt Thank You: To everyone who has supported me this year by purchasing my game, providing feedback, or creating content, I cannot thank you enough. Your encouragement has been invaluable. Special thanks to content creators who believed in my game early on and offered fantastic feedback—you have truly made a difference.
To the community supporting Rise of the Village Hero and my solo studio, Ludus Pax Studios, as well as my other projects like Rusty Hammer and Path to Serenity, I wish you all a wonderful holiday season. Enjoy this time with your friends and family, and may it be filled with joy and relaxation.
Holiday Break: I will be taking some time off to recharge and spend quality time with my wife and son. I plan to return on or around January 8th, ready to dive into Chapters 3 and 4 and work towards version 1.0 of the game.

Thank you again for your incredible support. Have a fantastic holiday season, and I’ll see you all in the new year!

Warm regards,
Silviu

notes.title: November End-of-Month Update: Experience balancing, new equipment, and more
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Thank you for your patience—it’s time for the end-of-November monthly update!

This update includes:
Experience balancing:
The experience gained from all enemies has been adjusted. Players will now receive less experience, allowing for a more balanced levelling process. This ensures enemies remain a challenge and aren’t too easy to defeat. Balancing experience gain took the most time during testing, as it required careful adjustments and extensive playthroughs to ensure character progression feels natural and enemies remain appropriately matched to the player's level. This is an ongoing process, so further refinements and testing will continue.

New equipment added:
Several new items have been introduced, including Golden Guard Gloves, Golden Guard Greaves, Scaled Fists, Padded Armour Set, Scaled Pants, and the incomplete Desolation of Glory Set. These and other items (some of which I can’t recall at the moment—sorry!) can now be found in shops, dropped randomly, or earned as quest rewards.

Shops stock:
Shops can now stock the newly added items. Additionally, if certain stores don’t sell some items, they can now buy them from the player character.

Quest bug fixes:
Fixed quest completion issues in the "Long Road to Wynter" area between Chapters 2 and 3.

New enemy class for elves:
A new enemy class has been created for elves. This should make them more balanced, particularly for those who choose the aggressive path.

Plans for December:
Expect another update in the first week of December, which will likely include:

More weapons and rewards.
Additional side quests.
An updated demo, potentially featuring a festive surprise!

After the early December update, I’ll be taking a break for the holidays to spend time with my family and recharge. There won’t be an end-of-month Christmas update. I plan to return refreshed in January to start work on Chapter 3, followed by Chapter 4 in February. Polishing and testing will then take place as I work towards reaching version 1.0.

Thank you so much for your continued support, for purchasing the game, and for being part of this journey. I truly appreciate it.

See you in the next update!

Silviu

notes.title: Patch Notes: November Update (Patches 1 & 2)
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

I’ve been hard at work improving the game following the release of the November update. After some testing, I identified a few things that needed adjustment. Below are the details for both the first patch and the recently released second patch.

Patch 1: Key Changes
- Dragonclaw (new dagger): The icon for Dragonclaw previously matched that of Omen. This has now been corrected.
- Omen description: The description was too similar to Orc Flesh Destroyer, so it has been updated for clarity.
- Grieving Blade & Blackout swap: Grieving Blade is now given by the farmer as a reward while Blackout is found elsewhere in the level.
- Oath of the Hunter set: Defence stats have been adjusted.
- Flameward Sword: Requirements to purchase have been reduced. You can now buy it from the lowest dungeon.
- Store updates: All stores now buy a broader range of items that players may accumulate.
- Potion prices: Prices for stamina, small health, and medium health potions have increased, and their descriptions have been updated.

Patch 2: Further Updates

Pirouette ability:
- Level 2 damage increased to 100.
- Level 3 damage increased to 150.
These changes make the ability more relevant when facing larger enemies in Chapter 2. These values may evolve as new abilities are added.
- Bug fix: In Cave Level 1, Chapter 2, the ground in the first spider area wasn’t correctly set to the “ground” layer. This has now been fixed.

Combat enhancement: 
- Additional goblins have been placed behind the trolls to increase the sense of urgency. Players now face added pressure to defeat the trolls quickly, or risk being overwhelmed.

Quest fix - "Long Road to Wynter": 
- Fixed an issue where Amber Blades weren’t triggering aggressive behavior during the quest. I’ll continue to monitor this to ensure the fix works as intended.

Notes
These patches should not affect your current save files as no enemy stats or major mechanics were altered.

Thank you all for your continuous support and feedback! I’ll keep testing and making improvements.

notes.title: November 1st update - Long road to Wynter quests, dialogues and more
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Welcome to another update! Let’s dive into what I’ve managed to accomplish so far:

First up, The Long Road to Wynter level is now fully complete in terms of design. It’s taken a while, but the terrain now looks exactly how I envisioned it. There may be some smaller elements of polish added over time, but for now, I’m happy with where it stands. All the dialogues and quests are also finished, and I’ve fully tested the pacifist branch. The aggressive path should work as well, but I’ll be running more tests over the weekend to confirm.

In terms of content, I’ve added more shields to the Cave System area in the Kingdom of Macin, specifically at the first shop in the Dwarven Assembly, located between Chapters 1 and 2. Additionally, I’ve added three new shields as rewards for completing pacifist quests in The Long Road to Wynter.  All the shields added include the Dancing Barricade, Broken Promise, Round Shield, Light Shield of the Lost, and Vengeance Wall.

I’ve also made some adjustments to daggers by lowering their damage and requirements. Three new daggers have been added—two of which are available both in the shop and as drops, and one that’s exclusively in the shop at the keep. These are Omen, Dragonclaw and Misty Glass.

As for armour, two incomplete silver sets have been introduced, currently missing only the chest pieces: Oath of the Hunter and Deflector of Assassins. They wont get a chest piece probably but that is OK. I want to have some incomplete sets as well. These are at the shop at keep as well as the random drop for 1 set.

Player leveling has also been adjusted to balance progression. Now, players will reach level 2 at 2,000 experience points. From level 2 to 10, each level requires 4,000 experience; from level 10 to 15, each level requires 6,000 experience; and from level 15 to 20, each level requires 8,000 experience. This should help maintain balance, though I’ll continue tweaking as new equipment and weapons are added.

Finally, I’ve been working on something special that I plan to release within the demo around the holidays! I can’t reveal too much just yet (as I want it to be a surprise), but expect a special event announcement sometime in December.

Due to changes in player leveling and adjustments to enemy levels, it's probably best to start a new save, as your old save may be affected by these updates. I can only apologise for the inconvenience, but with larger updates like this, some tweaks are unavoidable.

Thanks for reading, and I hope you all have a great end to the week. 
See you at the end of the month with my November final update.

Silviu

notes.title: October Month end Update
notes.content:
Update Notes - October Month end 

Hello!

I am excited to share some significant updates on my journey through Long Road to Wynter! A lot of new content and improvements have been added to enhance the experience, with more on the way. Here’s a summary of what you can expect in the latest update:

New area
Long Road to Wynter: This area is now open for exploration, battles, and quests. While much of it is still a work in progress, you’ll find various drops and some quests to tackle. More details on what’s to come are at the end of these notes. 

Abilities & Combat
Whirlpool Pirouette: Now available in levels 1-3, with enhanced animations and effects.
Combat Flow: Character speed and acceleration have been increased for a more dynamic experience, and enemies have larger hit colliders for easier targeting. Plus, the player will automatically face enemies when performing abilities, adding to the immersion.
Weapons additions: Several new weapons have been added, and some unique ones now drop from enemies. These can be used by the player, offering more variety and options in combat.

New Weapons
Dobroja’s Wrath: Found in the spider caves (Chapter 2, Level 2).
King’s Defender: Earned as a reward for completing the King’s Troll Demise quest.
The Untamed & Dawn: Found in the Long Road to Wynter area, located between Chapters 2 and 3.

Audio & Feedback Enhancements
Sound Effects for Equipping: Unique sound effects now play when equipping different types of armor and equipment to give players auditory feedback.
Potion Feedback: Sound effects now trigger when using potions, and no sound will play if a potion cant be used.
Ability Sounds: Custom sound effects have been added for abilities like Whirlpool, enhancing feedback when used successfully.
Health & Stamina Alerts: New audio cues play at half and critical levels, giving players more awareness during intense moments. (I recorded the voice myself. )

Improved Stat Descriptions & Bonuses
Charisma, Cunning, Dexterity Updates: Each attribute now has a clearer description and refined bonuses. This was something that was feedback before that some of the stats didnt offer clear explanation of what they did so hopefully this is much clearer. Major change is Willpower no longer handles bonuses on regeneration that is handled by Dexterity. Cunning offers bonuses on Defence.

New Daggers: Several new daggers have been added, enriching the arsenal for close-combat players, these are weapons that are also used by enemies so that is cool. 

Blacksmith Scene Completed: Ricker can now be found at the blacksmith, and he gives you som more goodies. 

Story Elements & Quest Additions
Additional Story Content: Look out for more story elements, like the ones near the caves and boss levels in the first chapter, that add depth and lore to the world and help me tell the story I wish to tell.

Future Quests: Planning to add quests in the areas between Chapters 2 and 3, including a link to White Shallows. Players choosing to ally with factions, such as the Elves, will have unique opportunities to tackle rival groups, including the Order of Obsidian Talons. Will try and add more depth as much as I can and to make sure that players decisions get carried over into future chapters. I am a solo dev so may not always be able to do it but I will try my best.

Coming Soon
Next month, I'll be focusing on even more quests in Long Road to Wynter as I continue to expand the area towards Chapter 3. 

I hope to release a small Halloween patch on October 31st to celebrate the spooky season, so stay tuned! But depends on how busy I am getting with work.

Thank you for your continued support, and see you on the Long Road to Wynter!

- Silviu

notes.title: October update Week 2 - New area, improvements to weapons and more
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Here are the details of October’s first update.

New Enemy Weapons: In this update, I’ve focused on enhancing the variety of weapons enemies wield. For the first chapter, orcs now have an expanded arsenal. In addition to their clubs and bows, they can be seen using two different types of daggers as well as a sword. This adds a fresh sense of variety to combat, which I think will be fun to experience.
Some of these new weapons have also been made available for the player and can be randomly dropped by enemies, depending on your luck and the random generation system.
New animations added for all daggers in the game for the player so this adds again a variety to combat.
I’ve also added new weapons for the Pig Chef of the trolls, along with a couple of weapon variations for the trolls themselves. I plan to continue adding more to ensure each enemy feels a little more unique.

New Area: A new area has been added for players to explore—the blacksmith shop in Warlington, owned by Rickon, the tutorial NPC. Without giving away too much, Rickon has changed his mind about something, and you’ll get to find out what when you talk to him there. Be sure to explore the shop—it contains a few goodies worth discovering!

New Ability: Whirlwind Pirouette (Level 1): Rickon now offers a special reward if you complete his first quest—he will teach you the game's first ability, Whirlwind Pirouette (Level 1). This ability is well worth unlocking, as it ads variety to the combat. While regular attacks still require small amount of stamina (1 point currently though this may change with testing), the majority is now used for abilities. If you’re out of stamina, though, you won’t be able to attack—so manage it wisely.
The Whirlwind Pirouette is an area-of-effect attack that damages enemies within a 2-meter radius. If there are no enemies nearby, or they aren’t within that range, the ability won’t activate. You’ll see a circular indicator showing the attack’s range, so it’s best to engage an enemy first before using the ability to maximize its effect. This ability is particularly useful when surrounded by enemies, allowing you to hit multiple foes at once.
I’m excited to introduce this mechanic into the game and look forward to adding more abilities soon! This should add a much needed variety to combat.

Bug Fixes:
Fixed a graphical glitch that occasionally occurred when loading a new game.
Added a longer fade to the title loading screen for a smoother transition.

Testing and Balancing: With the addition of new weapons and the abilities, I’ll be running more tests to ensure the gameplay remains balanced. I may need to adjust enemy levels accordingly, but so far, the early tests look promising!

Demo Updated: The demo has been updated to include the new blacksmith area, the ability from Rickon’s quest, and all the new weapons mentioned earlier. However, the new weapons won’t be available for purchase in the demo version—you’ll be able to buy/sell them in the early access version game, starting in the Dungeon level.

Thank you very much for your support and see you at the next update!

Silviu

notes.title: End of September Update
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Welcome to the end-of-September update! There's a lot to cover, so let's jump right in.

New Levels and Improvements:

New levels have been added to Chapter 2, including Underwater Cave Level 2 and the Underwater Cave Boss Level. I have added lighting to create a more immersive cave system look and built lighting for this.
Improvements have been made to both White Shallows and Underwater Cave Level 1, with more enemies and additional gates to block off areas until you have the necessary quests. Additionally new quests have been added to White Shallows which will link to the next area. These will be important to the replayability factor. Depends on which faction you chose. 

New Armor Sets:

The Fierce Chain Set can now be found around the White Shallows.
The Set of Conquered Sorrow has been added as a reward.
Two additional armor sets, Hope of the Crusader and Verdant Ward of Dobroja, are now part of the drop system.

New Weapons:

Three new swords have been added: Violet Reaper, Blind Justice, and Dobroja’s Wrath.

AI Improvements:

I've made updates to the AI for archers, making them run away from the player to create more diverse enemy behaviour. More of these hopefully in the future.

New Enemies:

Spiders have been introduced in Chapter 2, particularly in the Underwater Caves lvl 1 and lvl 2. These come in two types—green and red—and can be quite challenging.

Boss Level:

A new boss level has been added for the final underwater cave with its own boss, “Pig Chef”, a troll leader. This marks the end of chapter 2 and from here on players will see the "You Won" scene. More levels will be added however soon! 

Balancing:

All enemies and levels will undergo testing to ensure balance. If necessary, I’ll release patches to adjust difficulty. For now, I’ve added more potions to help players. These will be balanced over time.

Story Enhancements:

I've added new story elements to give more depth and context to the world. These are designed to work alongside dialogue and quests, enriching the narrative and encouraging exploration. They act as scrolls that players can read as they are found. More will be added as I continue developing the levels.

Markers for Navigation:

To assist players who may feel lost, I've introduced new looping visual markers that point towards exits and key locations.

UI and Menu Improvements:

The UI has been improved overall, and the pause menu now includes new buttons. I've also added an option to quit without saving, for those who prefer not to save their progress.

Tier System Updates:

The tier system, introduced earlier this month, has been refined. There are now 5 tiers: Grey, Green, Blue, Light Gold, and Gold. More tiers will be added in future updates.

Testing and Next Steps:

I'll be spending this week conducting extensive tests to ensure the game build is working as intended and its overall balanced. I have already done quite a lot of this past 3 weeks in Unity directly but its easier sometimes to do it in Steam. If everything is fine, I'll move on to developing the next area and adding more story elements.

If any patches are required to fix issues, I apologise in advance. I always aim to ensure everything works smoothly, so if you see an update icon, please make sure to update the game first. It shouldn’t affect your save files.

Thank you very much for your support and for your patience.

Silviu

notes.title: September: Week 1 patch update
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Thank you all for your patience. This patch includes several small improvements to enhance the overall gameplay experience:


 Doors added in Warlington (Chapter 1, First Level): These doors (Portcullis for castle gates) have been introduced to encourage players to fully explore the starting area and obtain the main quest. This helps with the storytelling and ensures that players don’t accidentally disrupt the game flow by attacking enemies linked to quests, before receiving their quest, which previously caused the "ghosts that attack you but you can't attack them" bug.
 Increased stock in the shop in the Kingdom of Macin (Cave level between Chapter 1 and Chapter 2): The shopkeeper now can purchase most of your items. Potions have also been added to the shop to assist players who may need them at this stage.
 Additional door before the final area: A new door has been placed to prevent access to the final area of the map until players have completed the quest Dwarven Uprising Part 2. This is to ensure that the quest progression remains intact.
 Removed duplicate equipment in Chapter 2 (White Shallows): There was an issue where a piece of equipment could be both found on the ground and received as a reward. This duplication has been fixed.
 Adjusted enemies in Chapter 2: More enemies have been added to the Cave Trolls level (Level 1), while the knights in the White Shallows (Chapter 2, Level 1) have been slightly nerfed for balance.
 Improved skeleton animations: Skeletons now use humanoid animations instead of the shared orc/goblin animators, giving them a more appropriate feel. Trying to use a mixture of them ended up causing the *ghost reanimated bug* which doesnt attack the player but when reloading the game they enemies oddly stand up.
 More health drops in Chapter 2: Additional health drops have been scattered throughout Chapter 2 to help with the balance.
 I had to release a couple of patches today as there were a few small issues that weren't quite working. However, the main addons, such as doors mechanic and animations, are now functioning as intended now.


I'll continue testing to ensure the game remains balanced, including assessing player levels versus enemies and the availability of health pickups in the coming days. Thanks again for your feedback and support!
I’ll aim to release more content soon not sure if weekly but I will try; with a primary focus on completing Chapter 2 and progressing to the next area. I’m also considering adding more equipment, adding them to the stores and around the world and drop mechanic.

This week’s update does not affect save files—I’ve checked, and I can still play with my old save.

Thank you for your continued support, and see you in the next update!
Silviu

notes.title: August Update: UI Overhaul, New Interiors, and More!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!
The August update brings significant improvements to the game, particularly in the UI and gameplay experience.

UI Enhancements:
•	Shop UI: I’ve revamped the shop interface to offer a cleaner look and better showcase items. Everything is more centred, and item names now fit nicely for improved presentation.
•	Dialogue UI: I’ve made some adjustments to the dialogue interface, giving it a slight visual upgrade. This is still a work in progress, but it’s looking better for now.
•	Inventory & Character Sheet: These have been combined into one interface. Now, pressing "Tab" will open the inventory and give you access to skill points. The UI has been refined to make equipped items stand out, with everything better aligned and centred. I’ve also started working on a new type of equipment—rings. There are two extra slots available, though one might change to a belt in future updates.
•	Quest UI: The quest interface has been improved, with the quest background made more prominent. An exclamation mark has been added to the quest book icon, making it easier to spot.
•	Pause Menu UI: The pause menu has been updated with a couple of new buttons. There’s now a "Controls" button for quick access to the game’s controls key. Additionally, a "Quit" button has been added, allowing you to exit without saving. This is useful if you want to restart from the last auto-save point.

Pickups:
Pickups have been updated to make item tiers more visible. Now, when you see an item, its name will be clearly displayed, helping you decide whether to keep it or leave it. Its name will be coloured based on its rank with silver/white tier 1, green tier 2, and so on. This change makes it easier to distinguish between different tiers of weapons and gear. Currently, there are five tiers, with more likely to come in future updates.

New Interior Scenes:
In the previous update, I introduced a house to explore in the first level. Now, I’ve added an explorable church interior, which changes how the main quest unfolds. You can now enter the church, aligning more closely with the game’s narrative and vision. The church also leads to dungeons as you progress through the game.

Demo Update:
The demo will be updated to include all the changes mentioned above, plus the new church scene. This should increase the overall playtime. The demo will soon feature Warlington Town, the Church scene (which concludes the demo), and the house interior.


Other smaller improvements:
•	Cinematic Intro: The cinematic intro at the start of the first level has been edited for a better way of showing points of interest, also it was shortened.
•	Lighting Enhancements: Earlier this month, I improved the lighting across all levels, which complements the current update.
•	Combat Improvements: You can now attack and take potions simultaneously, allowing you to heal while staying engaged in combat.This was again released in the middle of the month.


Studio News:
I recently attended the Glasgow World Conference, where I had the opportunity to showcase my studio’s work and my game, Rise of the Village Hero. The event lasted five days, and it was an incredible experience to present the game to a wider audience. Seeing people play my game live again was awesome!

Thank you for checking out the August update! I’ll start working on the plan for the September update as soon as this one is released. I hope you enjoy the new features, and I look forward to sharing more in the next update.

See you soon!
Silviu

notes.title: Rise of the Village Hero - July Update
notes.content:
July Update Notes
This month, I've focused on enhancing the game through a series of updates and improvements across various categories. I focused primarily on testing stats for player and enemies and bosses and resources such as potions. Here’s a detailed breakdown of what has been tackled and improved in July:
Shops and Items
1.	Inventory Additions:
o	I have updated the shops throughout the dungeons and Warlington to ensure they buy whatever the player may have on him at the time.
2.	Dungeon Shop Adjustments:
o	Lowest dungeon: Removed small health potions, added 10-20 medium health potions.
o	Last shop after boss now buys items that I added that may not have.
3.	Item Adjustments:
o	Created and named three new swords: "Blade of Dobroja Blue Sword," "Knights Valor," "Dobroja's Wrath."
o	Ensured last shops buy Chaos, Rusty Sword, Razorwind.
o	Removed leather greaves from the lowest dungeon floor.
o	Swapped rewards for saving NPC and checked for Lucky Tooth reward consistency.
Character and Enemy Levels
1.	Level enemy adjustments based on tests:
o	Increased Wizzard Necromancer boss’s level by 2.
o	Increased cook trolls' level by 2.
o	Adjusted trolls' levels based on players health for appropriate balancing.
o	Adjusted orc bandits and shaman levels in Meadows by decreasing them by 1.
o	Increased necromancer boss level by 2.
o	Increased final boss level by 1.
o	Adjusted skeleton levels in Caves: Brotherly Rescue quest (united vision for bridge skeletons, increased one skeleton by 1 level, increased helper by 1 level).
o	Increased skeleton levels in "Stop Ritual" quest by 1 or 2.
o	Leveled up skeleton next to chest in Caves by 2.
o	Verified and fixed missing NPC saving quest with unique ID, rewarded with the worst pendant.
o	Adjusted soldiers near abandoned camp by downgrading their level by 1 and increasing their range for group combat.


Testing and Fixing Visual Elements
1.	Navigation and Map:
o	Implemented nav mesh in Chapter 2 on itch.io update.
o	Added map hints in Kingdom of Macin, Chapter 1, and Meadows with new UI for location guidance.
2.	Environmental adjustments and visual fixes:
o	Recreated a similar waterfall from Caves in White Shallows.
o	Made statue in White Shallows marketplace static to prevent walking through. Same statues were removed from the Warlington square for creating odd light reflections.
o	Fixed the visible floor issue behind the ghost husband in the lower dungeon.

3.	Health Potions and Quests:
o	Added more health potions and quests to White Shallows.
o	Ensured medium health potions are sold by the potion seller in the dungeon level before the boss.
Additional Improvements
1.	Environmental and Aesthetic Enhancements:
o	Tomb kings of Macin: Added new tombs next to each other to represent previous kings and their spouses. Future plans include a small UI detailing each ruling family's history.
o	Kings Hall: Added additional assets and banners, showing visible damage.
o	Assembly: Transformed the area where the fountain was into an assembly area, symbolizing where lords once sat.
o	Marketplace of Kingdom of Macin: Added a marketplace at the bottom of the steps from Kings Hall, next to the waterfall.
2.	Gameplay and Narrative Adjustments:
o	Removed food reward for completing Chapter 2, upon completion of the quest.
o	Ensured proper quest flow for "Stop Ritual" and "Brotherly Rescue," including adjusted skeleton and helper levels.
3.	New Features:
o	Map Hints: Added in Kingdom of Macin, Chapter 1, and Meadows with new UI for location guidance. For example, the tutorial man at the front of Warlington Castle tells you survivors have taken refuge in the small Keep, and the map hint guides you there.
o	Interior Exploration: For the first time, added the ability to explore inside homes. One house is now explorable, - in Warlington first level- with more to be added in future updates. This changes navigation to dungeon levels, with a new interior scene for the Church planned for the next update to improve quest navigation and scene breakdown.

Thank you for your patience its been a challenging month as I had limited time to work on the game since summer holidays and all but happy with the update I was able to release, and will see you all at the next update in August. 

As always if you have any feedback press F12 and drop a feedback form it will get to my trello!

Thank you to anyone who wishlisted my game and purchased it I greatly appreciate your support and helping me live my dream.

Silviu
Creator of Rise of the Village Hero 
and Founder of solo dev studio Ludus Pax Studios

notes.title: June: Update 5C Overall improvements and feedback implementation
notes.content:
Hi there!

Welcome to the June update. This month, I've been focusing on the valuable feedback from play testers, content creators, and the wider community. I've updated my Trello board to incorporate these suggestions and have been hard at work addressing them.
I received a less favourable review from a publication. While I don't agree with every point, I’ve taken as much on board as possible. Constructive criticism is part of the journey, and I'm committed to improving the game.
Also, as always, it’s advisable to start a new game with a new save, at every update to avoid any issues in saving.
I will be testing the game for next couple of days and if I notice anything out of the ordinary will most likely release a quick update patch to fix any irregularities. 

With monthly updates planned, I aim to enhance and expand the game continuously. Here are some of the changes and improvements based on feedback:

Feedback from Players, Creators, and Press:

Using ranged weapons is difficult and lacks impact on combat:
Ranged weapons require accuracy, which is challenging to balance. I’ve increased the damage of the three bows available in the game:
Tranquility: Obtainable by allying with the Goblin Conglomerate.
Ironbark: Found next to a certain brave and humble farmer.
Razorwind: Reward for the first quest of Chapter 1 – Part 1.
More bows are intended to be added to the game for sure to add that option for players who are looking to play range. 

Skills lack clear explanations:
I’ve added a tool to explain how each point affects your character's stats. This was a frequent request and something I’ve wanted to implement for a while.

Shop purchases are less useful and there aren't enough shops:
I’ve added a new shop in the lowest dungeon (level 4 before the boss fight) and expanded the inventory of existing shops. More shops and items will be added in future updates, including a shop in the cave system.

Not enough health potions; small and medium don’t offer enough:
I’ve increased the effectiveness of small and medium health potions and adjusted their prices accordingly.

Bosses are too easy to defeat:
Balancing boss difficulty is ongoing. I’ve reworked the levels of enemies and bosses in Chapter 1 and the interlink area to provide a more challenging experience without causing frustration.

Experience UI is not present:
The experience UI was too transparent, so I’ve made it fully coloured for better visibility. I’m continuously working on improving the UI.

Environment feels sparse, with more trees than proper buildings:
I’m enhancing the environment, especially in Chapter 2, by adding more buildings where appropriate, such as warehouses in White Shallows forest.

All items on the ground look the same; no variety:
I’ve ensured that drops now reflect the actual items, like swords, instead of default bags. I’ll extend this to armour in future updates.

Grammar mistakes:
I’ve corrected various grammatical errors and inconsistencies in the dialogue. English is my second language, but I strive to correct mistakes as soon as I notice them.

Slots are not in the correct order for equipment:
I’ve reorganized the equipment slots in the UI to make them more intuitive for players.

Path to Development 1.0:

Variation of enemies:
I’ve added animals like wolves and -soon bears -to the biomes, providing more quest opportunities, combat variety.

Equipment:
Six new swords have been added:

Scar: A green sword.
Oblivion: A blue sword.
Venom and Frost Sword: Two light gold swords.
Brutality and Blind Justice: Gold swords.
Prices have been adjusted to balance the amount of gold players accumulate.

New Armor Set:
Two new set of armours each of five pieces. Fierce Chainmail armor pieces has been added, though they still need to be placed in shops.Hope of Crusader set has been added into the White Shallows area.

Overall Testing:
I’ve rebalanced player and enemy levels and adjusted the experience required to level up. Players now level up after 2,000 experience points initially and then every 4,000 points thereafter.

Chapter 2 – White Shallows and Underwater Cave level 1:
I’ve improved these levels, making them more engaging and detailed. The “Early Access warning” for White Shallows will remain until I add more quests and dialogues are added and I am happy to move it to the next area.

Thank you so much for your support, wishlisting my game, playing it, and providing feedback. It means the world to me. The next update will be in July, followed by August. These updates may be smaller as I’ll be spending time with my child during the summer holidays.

Thank you again for your continued support.

Silviu
Founder of Solo Studio Ludus Pax Studios
Creator of Rise of the Village Hero

notes.title: May: Update 2 - 5B
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Thank you for your patience; here is the May update number 2! This update features a new area, bug fixes, and overall game improvements. I am excited to release this update. As always it is always best to start a new save when an update is released to avoid any unexpected save issues. 

In the last update, I introduced the first level of Chapter 2—White Shallows. This area includes the town of White Shallows and its surrounding areas, such as farming regions. In this update, overall improvements have been made to the effects and level design. More enemies have been added. Currently, only a couple of quests are present, but expect more quests and dialogue to be added to this region, making it more worthwhile to explore. This area is perfect for introducing animals as enemies or simple NPCs, although I didn't manage to include them in this update.

The second level is the first Underwater Cave, marking the second level of Chapter 2. The player needs to find the villagers who have been kidnapped by trolls, ideally before they are turned into dinner. This level is complete with props, and significant work has been done to make it unique and worth exploring. More props, quests, and dialogues will be added in future updates. Currently, the quest to save the villagers can be completed, but more unique NPCs will be added.

Bug fixes and game improvements:

 One of the most annoying issues in combat was that projectiles could pass through walls, castles, houses, etc. This has now been fixed. I am very happy about this because it means players can take a moment to strategise, heal, and then deal with the monsters.

 All enemies have had their vision edited. This means that, in theory, no enemy should see the player character through a wall and start chasing them from a different room. Enemies will now only see the player if they step into the same room, rather than chasing from behind a thick wall.

This brings us to the end of this update. Adding a new level and improving the previous one has taken a lot longer than expected. I look forward to adding more to these two levels in the next update and removing the "From here on out there may be bugs" notice, moving it to the next level.

I hope to add the last two levels in the next updates in June and then focus on polishing Chapter 2 and other areas for a month or so. This would mean the game is halfway through development, which is a great milestone.

Quick recap: when the game launched in early access in January 2024, it included:

Chapter 1: Village up to Boss level (5 levels)
Interlink area between Chapter 1 and Chapter 2 (2 levels, not finished at the time)
This initially provided about 3.5 hours of content. Improvements over the last few months should make this longer. Since Update 5.A, Chapter 2 – White Shallow level has been added, and now with 5.B, Underwater Caves have been added to the build, bringing the total content to around 4-5 hours. Chapter 1 an interlink area to chapter 2 are fully completed.

Two more levels need to be added to Chapter 2 before finishing this chapter. Future content to be added includes:

Interlink area between Chapter 2 and Chapter 3
Chapter 3
Interlink area between Chapter 3 and Chapter 4
Final Chapter 4 – where the game’s story will come to fruition and final boss will be revealed. 

Thank you to everyone who has purchased the game or supported it with a wishlist. I really appreciate it.

See you in the next update!

notes.title: May 1st Update 5A
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Can you believe it's already May? I can't believe how fast time has passed. Today is May 16th, which means it's update day. The next update to look forward to will be on the 31st of this month. Although this update may not affect your save. I would recommend most times to start a new game just as a new save to ensure no bugs surface.
I would like to thank you all for your support and consideration, whether you've purchased my game or wishlisted it. You are making my solo dev dream possible. I really mean it. I wouldn’t be able to do what I do without your support, so for that, I am forever grateful. Let's jump into the update information.

In this update, I focused mostly on improving and overhauling the sound effects of all enemies and players, as well as adding a new area called White Shallows, which is the first level of Chapter 2. It's quite a big level, so please be patient as more side quests will be added, enemies, etc.
Here are the points that this update has focused on in more detail:


Interlinking area between Chapter 1 (Ch 1) to Chapter 2 (Ch 2) has been finished. All quests have been linked between each other, and NPCs' dialogue and everything works accordingly. This has allowed me to remove the “Early access notice” and move it to Ch 2, White Shallows' first level.
Improvements have been made to all present enemies and player sound effects for being hit and dying, including Skeleton class, Orc class, and Ghost class (along with all their individual subclasses).
 Extensive Save system debugging, and fixes have been done in terms of NPCs' locations, and a different way to open doors based on quest completion has been implemented. (Not necessarily something noticeable to you, the player, but important for my ability to tell the story and create variations).
I added a new type of enemy class to the White Shallows and added all the NPCs, as well as quests to the level. Quests are playable, and one quest is dependent on what quest you have from previous levels, creating a nice link of the player’s choice.
I added 10 pieces of new armour equipment (5 of which have already been added to the quest rewards and some have been placed around the level).
Improved overall rewards in the game, making sure that most quests offer the players reasonable rewards, worthwhile of players' effort instead of just gold pieces.
Edited all the spawns to health potions from level 3 and above to medium health potions to ensure that the player can replenish their health adequately and doesn’t run out, without forcing the players to have to travel back to traders unless they wish to do so.


Thank you again for your patience and support. I will continue to work hard, and I will start setting up my targets on my Trello board for the remainder of the month. 

If you run into any issues, as usual, please consider pressing F12 and giving either feedback or submitting a bug if you discover one. Anything you think should have happened? Is this normal? Just press F12; it will take a screenshot and send it over to my Trello board so I can investigate it. Every PC is different, and there is no way for me to know how the game may play on every single setup. So, your help is greatly appreciated. 

If you like consider joining my discord here: https://discord.gg/gTcyg8mFfF 

Thank you again for your support!

notes.title: April Update 4G Part 2
notes.content:
Hello,

Thank you for your patience and your support.

Today, I have released an update this morning, and this is a slight patch to that. This update covered the following aspects:


 I conducted an inventory of all the equipment, allowing me to note which were used and which were not.
 I started using those that were not placed in the world.
 Additionally, I began changing the inventory items so that players receive not just gold, but also decent items as rewards for completing quests.
 I started working on editing the different dialogue options for secondary quests to ensure that players have various choices.
 Farmer quests, noble lady quests, and the pacifist or aggressive paths for the Goblin conglomerate should work as intended and not be reset by the save/load functionality.
 I edited the shops to reflect the new inventory that the keep should have and the dungeon goblin merchant.
 I have fixed an issue with the Meadow and Cave levels in the interlink areas between chapters 1 and 2, where gates would be reset.
 I managed to make it consistent when loading or continuing the game. This final fix allows me to tell my story by being able to lock areas if a quest is not complete.
 This is essential for how I wanted the story to be told but had struggled to incorporate it into the save system. Now that it's fixed, I will continue to work on improving it.


I will continue to tackle in the next few days:


 Adding more rewards to different quests.
 I will start adding medium health potions from level 3 dungeon onwards, replacing small health potions. Incorporating some form of additional healing options such as fountains might be a good idea too.If changing to medium potions earlier is not a fix. This suggestion came from feedback I received recently from a player.
 I will start finishing up the quests in the Cave level (from the interlinking area between chapter 1 and 2) and then start focusing on Chapter 2. Really exciting time indeed.


Many challenges lie ahead for me as a solo dev, but I am really enjoying the journey. I shall continue to work hard to make the game as good as I can. Thank you for your patience and support. 

Silviu
Game developer of Rise of the Village Hero
Founder of Ludus Pax Studios

notes.title: April update - 4G1
notes.content:
Hey all, thank you for patiently waiting. I've been hard at work on the game over the last 3-4 days since I have submitted all my uni assessments, and I'm excited to share the latest update. This update addresses some small bugs and includes a significant improvement in frames per second in Warlington town. The drop in frame rate was only experienced on some machines, including mine, but it was due to the fog, which has now been rectified.

Small bug fixes:

- Fixed the sound effect for the Blackout sword.
- Edited dialogue for the lady farmer, whose farm is being attacked by deserter orcs.
- Fixed her house so players can no longer access it by walking through the walls.

Big bug fixes:

- Improved frames per second in Warlington town (first scene) to now over 60 FPS.

Aesthetics:

- Added a new set of armor called Knight Leather armor.
- Added more assets to the roster of armor and more amulets. These will be added later to the dropper 
  and quests. More of these will continue to be added to increase the inventory and randomize the 
  options.
- The farmer lady's house in the Meadow level is now fully furnished.
- Started working on improving lighting in Warlington town, as Guy is supposed to arrive at night, so I 
  made the scene darker.
- Added more amulets, which will serve as rewards in some quests.
- Modeled an amulet for the first amulet of health so players will now be able to see an amulet instead 
  of a bag when they drop it on the ground.
- Fixed the default drop; sometimes it would fall to the ground, but now it should always be above 
  ground.
- Added slight fog in the first scene town of Warlington.
- Made improvements to the attack system by adding a sound effect to showcase lack of stamina.
- Improved the level up FX to make it more obvious that the player has leveled up. This addition has 
  been made based on feedback.

Thank you for reading!

notes.title: March - Update 4.F1 Part 1
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

I just wanted to provide an update notice as I have released a couple of updates on March 7th.

Following some feedback from players, I have decided to release an update to address some things. Here are the main points of the update:

- Improved attack accuracy by addressing the interference that the UI from enemies caused when clicked on. I have made it so that the text damage no longer interferes with the attacks as it used to. I had noticed that and now I managed to fix it. This has improved attack accuracy when clicking on enemies and reduces miss clicking.

- I have added a tutorial quest. This tutorial quest introduces players to dialogue and quests and how they work. It also introduces players to equipment, potions, and stamina, and explains how to allocate skill points to your character. This should help players by giving them an introduction to the main game mechanics. I am considering expanding this further to offer more guidance to players.
Please find below my video of the showcase of the Tutorial quest on my YouTube channel:

[previewyoutube=A-WvY9m3EQ0;full][/previewyoutube]

From observing different players/content creators play my game, I noticed a couple of things that needed fixing, so here they are.

Bug fixes:

- Duplication of potions: This bug meant that quick saving/quick loading (F2/F3) would duplicate your potions in the action bar (1-6 bar where you place your potions for quick use). This bug has now been remedied.
- Big enemy (Orc captain): Now no longer interacts with the players unless they have the adequate quest to stop the enemy from breaking, as they are tied to a quest. Making them impossible to kill.

- Enemy next to the underground tunnel next to the church: Now has a similar tie to the quest, so players will have to explore and find the right quest.

Thank you for supporting my game by wishlisting, considering purchasing it, or purchasing it. I will continue to strive to make the game as good as I can. Thank you for supporting my solo indie dev dream.

PS - This month is a bit hectic with my Uni work so I was able to make this update and will see about releasing another one towards the end of the month but after first of April all my assessments are done and will be only focusing on my solo dev studio and Rise of the Village Hero so I am excited about this journey.

Silviu
Creator of Rise of the Village Hero
Founder of Ludus Pax Studios

notes.title: February Update 4.E1 : Patch 2
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

After watching the livestream the other day of one of the streamers who kindly played my game, I was able to observe and notice many things that I hadn't seen before. As a solo developer, I haven't had the chance to extensively test my game beyond players at PlayExpo Glasgow and a few friends. Since then, I've kept adding and modifying things.

Last night, I had the opportunity to observe a player who perhaps wasn't very familiar with my game, and it was a great learning experience. I needed to watch this so I could understand how other players might experience my game.

This patch addresses some issues that I identified during the stream:


 Improved UI to prevent the inventory from being dragged and moved left or right, fixing the bug I encountered last night when an item got stuck on the screen.
 Sliced properties enabled on all UI tabs to make it cleaner and more visually appealing.
 Improved dialogue UI boxes and art.
 Added Grieving Blades and several other items to the shops, which I seemed to have missed previously.
 The goblin merchant in the Dungeon level now buys almost everything from you to prevent players from having a full inventory in future levels.
 If you kill the ghosties that are unhappy with one another, the quest markers disappear.
 Increased the inventory size to 18 for better symmetry and visual appeal.
 Enhanced health drops in the first level to give newcomers an extra chance.
 Increased the levels of some mini-bosses in later levels to make them more resilient as players progress.
 Made small aesthetic changes to the boss level; final merchants can now buy most items to clear players' inventories for the next levels.
 Fixed a bug in the meadows where players could backtrack and spawn at the end of the final level (currently mines).
 Adjusted cave skeleton enemies to make the fight more challenging for players around level 12 or so.


Join my Discord here and join the conversation:
https://discord.gg/xnBVp9pBSs

I will continue to release updates and patches to my game as often as I can. Just a heads up that next month may be a little challenging because I am approaching the final few weeks of submission for my dissertation and final assessments at University (I am in my final years of Uni studying Games Development in Scotland). After that, all I will do is work on my game and studio! So updates/patches next month may be smaller, but after that, they will start increasing in size as I focus solely on my studio and game.

Thank you for playing my game, wishlisting it, reading my posts—anything really! I appreciate the support.

Silviu
Creator of Rise of the Village Hero
Founder of Ludus Pax Studios

notes.title: February Update 4.E1 : Patch 1
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

As promised, I will always try to release a bigger update once per month (that was released at the beginning of February or end of Jan) and two smaller patches throughout the month. These changes include some aesthetic updates and adjustments based on my gameplay testing on my YouTube channel, which you can find here: 
[previewyoutube=V8J9hVVMuCM;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]











During this gameplay testing, I made several observations:

- Addressed the issue of some objects in the lower dungeons not having a built navigation mesh.
- Increased the availability of stamina for purchase from shops (Dungeon shop and keep - in Village).
- Added daggers to the random dropper and left them available for purchase/sale in shops as well. I just felt that the daggers could come in handy earlier on in the combat rather than being bought later after that. (Some of this was done during my live stream of game dev and further edited in today's patch)
- Introduced health potions for sale at the dungeon goblin shop.
- Reduced the amount of stamina drops after level 7 as the regeneration felt fast enough.
- Moved up the drop levels for the Grieving Blade and Blackout (silver swords) as they were dropping too late in the game.
- Expanded the number of sound effects in the project (Just purchased a big pack of music and sound effects for the game's purpose). Changed some of the sound effects for silver/green/blue and gold swords to create variations. I had started this in the previous big update but went further with it this time. The orcs' melee weapons also have their own "woosh" sound effects.
- Added a sound effect for the caves' music. More will be added soon.
- Introduced two new extra bows for players who prefer ranged combat. The "player's bow," as it used to be called, has been given a proper name - Tranquility. The other two new ones are Ironbark and Razorwind. All of them are silver bows. More will be added in the future. I need to start making some of my own, or find more bow assets to buy.

This concludes the patch for now, but I will continue working on it for the next couple of weeks and add a few more changes hopefully before the end of the month. These updates should become bigger once Uni is wrapped up.

Thank you for reading my posts, for purchasing and for wishlisting and supporting me on my game dev journey.

If you want to chat and make suggestions on the game feel free to join my discord server here:
https://discord.gg/7PGnapaqqk

Thank you again!

notes.title: Small patch and update
notes.content:
Hello!

I have decided to make some changes which hopefully will improve the overall look and experience in my game. I am looking forward to feedback if these are not welcomed changes.

Aesthetic small update:

Quite a few areas around the "Village" level were just empty so I decided to place flowers and some flora around also changed the grass to something nicer in different parts of the level. 
I am quite happy how things look now as you can see from the screenshots they just look much better and nicer. 

Gameplay small update

Without knowing how things are perceived by players (due to lack of feedback) I can only look at player time in game. So I have drawn some conclusions based on what could perhaps cause frustrations.

So I am going to break down some parts of the game:

 When initiating combat you just need to click on the enemy once! This will lock you in with that enemy. You dont need to smash the button on the mouse. One time you click on it until the enemy is defeated. Or until you change enemy and your character moves to that enemy.
 Frames per second, in first level is between 35-45 (at least on my machine again due to lack of feedback I dont know how the first level is for others), very rarely dropping under 30. This is not something I can change though I have tried my best to optimise things in this level. I can only assume that because of the number of AI enemies, the number of assets and number of quests, dialogues etc things are a bit slowed down. I only ask for your patience please, all my other levels are 120 fps and above. So if you get into the dungeon level you will see a major improvement in frames per second.
 Game difficulty (Again due to lack of feedback not sure if its too hard or too easy) I have played it for hours but I am the developer. So one thing I would say is please drop feedback in the form. I will alter things accordingly. For now I have done a couple of changes. First interaction fight I have removed one of the enemies at the gate. This should leave players with a lot more of their health. I have also left the players an increase in health potions from 5 to 15. Hopefully that improves things. I have changed the original sword to one that you can equip without changing the strength in the character sheet. This should allow you to equip straight away a weapon. Ready for combat. 
Please read description of weapons they will tell you the requirements if any for, weapons, amulets, helmets shields etc.Press CTRL to add your skill points. If you dont have any more you found a weapon thats not ready to be equipped at your level. Congratulations the gods of random dropper were good to you :) 
 Game-play interruptions: 
After the main menu there is a cinematic this 1 min 20 seconds. After that in the first area there was a short cutscene showing points of interests. I have removed this. I am afraid in case this breaks the gameplay too much and ads further frustration. This short cutscene was meant to show players points of interests. For now I turned it off. I am waiting for feedback.
 Demo being added:
I want to add a demo on steam here. So that players can have a play of my game first and get comfortable and understand the mechanics before they make a purchase or decide to wishlist it.
Hoping this will get players more comfortable with mechanics type of story etc.

I hope this patch is helpful and gives you an idea that I am determined to make the game better improve it as much as I can.

Thank you for your patience and support.

Silviu 
Creator of Rise of the Village Hero
